_what: The slur list D18 requires. Read by tools/content-gate.py and by nothing else.
_why_it_is_a_file_and_not_code: So that it can be audited as one artifact, edited without touching the
gate's logic, and so the gate's own source does not read as a slur list.
It is NOT obfuscated. An encoded word list is an instrument nobody can
check, which is worse than an unpleasant one.
_the_boundary_D18_draws: FULL PERIOD SWEARING IS ALLOWED. Bloody, bastard, bugger, sod, shite,
arse, arsehole, piss off, bollocks, wanker, twat, git, prick, tosser,
berk, pillock, knobhead, fuck and cunt are SWEARING and this list does
not contain them. A gate that flagged profanity would be wrong against
the rule as given, and a writer who hit one would learn to route around
WHAT IS BARRED IS A SLUR: a word whose work is to demean a person for
the group they belong to. Race, nationality, ethnicity, religion and
THE HARDEST CASE IS 'cunt', and it is decided rather than overlooked.
In British usage of this period it is a general insult applied to men
far more often than a gendered attack, which is what makes it swearing
under the rule rather than a slur. It is left OUT of this list and
named in the report so the call is visible and can be reversed in one
line by adding it to `slurs` below.
_words_excluded_on_purpose_and_why: mick: MICKEY'S IS THE PUB AND MICKEY IS THE DEAD UNCLE. Mick is also
one of the commonest British first names of the period. Word-boundary
matching keeps 'Mickey' safe, but 'Mick' the name is not, so the word
is not listed at all. This one refusal would have hit canon.
paddy: an Irish first name, and 'throwing a paddy' is period slang for
spade, chink, frog, jock, tinker, gypsy, coloured, cripple, queer:
each has a live innocent sense in this register (a garden spade, a
chink of light, an animal, a Scottish name, to tinker with, a real
ethnonym, coloured glass, a crippled ship, a queer turn meaning odd).
Not listed. THIS IS AN ADMITTED UNDER-CATCH: a writer who uses one of
these in the demeaning sense passes the gate, and only a reader
catches it. Under-catching beats mangling ordinary dialogue.
tom: PERIOD POLICE SLANG FOR A PROSTITUTE AND THE PLAYER'S OWN NAME.
Never listed anywhere in this repo, in this list or the prostitution
rules. It is recorded here because somebody will propose it.
nip: 'nip out', 'a nip in the air' and 'nip round' are all ordinary period British. Not listed, and named here so nobody adds it without reading this line.
_how_to_edit: Add the narrowest word that does the demeaning work, lower case. Every
entry is matched WORD-BOUNDED and case-insensitively over spoken text,
so an entry that is a substring of an ordinary word is safe, but an
entry that IS an ordinary word is not. Run --selftest after editing:
the accepting half runs a line of period swearing through the scanner
